files.description: The rules of the repository: layout, dependency direction, codec tiers and the licence line, core design rules, workflow, testing expectations, writing style
The architecture: crate topology, backend tiers, pipeline model, defaults policy, CLI surface, metadata policy
The licence allow-list and the banned crates that cargo deny enforces
The CLI grammar: flags, path handling, output placement, feedback channels, exit codes
Which crate backs each native feature, why not jpegxl-rs, what each needs at build time
HEIC through ImageIO, WIC and a runtime-loaded libheif; the three binding crates that hold the workspace's unsafe
The cargo-dist release matrix, the per-target native set and the Homebrew tap
The colour stage: moxcms, the order of the pipeline stages, what keep_icc does
How --jobs is bounded: per-mode memory estimates, three quarters of available memory, the cgroup walk, the oversized-file warning
The resize interface: --width, --height, --fit, --position, --background, --scale, --enlarge, --filter in CSS object-fit terms, never enlarge by default, the width list for srcset
A type per pipeline stage: Sqzer::prepare gives a Prepared, Prepared::resize a Ready, encode takes a Ready; --fit outside; a translucent background needs an encoder with alpha

The browser build: portable means runs everywhere and may need a C compiler to build, oxipng on wasm32 through freestanding, AVIF decoding through the sqzer-rav1d fork on every target, the JavaScript API of sqzer-wasm with the browser's canvas as input fallback, simd128, the dist publish job for npm, the page in its own repository

Palette reduction for PNG: png:colors and png:dither through quantizr inside the PNG encoder, an image with few enough colours left exact, CodecOption::lossy and Output::lossless for an option that gives up pixels at a lossless target, the refusal of such an option together with a lossless target
